chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja‘far ibn Bashir, from Fudayl, from Tahir, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
Abu Abdullah عليه السلام used to blame Abdullah, reproach him, admonish him, and say: “What has prevented you from being like your brother? For by Allah, I surely recognize the light in his face.”
So Abdullah said: “Why? Is not my father and his father one, and my mother and his mother one?” So Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said to him: “Indeed, he is from my very self, while you are my son.”

key_terms.ابْنِي: my son; indicating ordinary filial relation in contrast to the former expression
key_terms.النُّورَ: the spiritual light recognized in his face
key_terms.مِنْ نَفْسِي: from my very self; expressing exceptional nearness
key_terms.وَجْهِهِ: his face, as the place where that light was seen
key_terms.يَعِظُهُ: he was admonishing and exhorting him
key_terms.يُعَاتِبُهُ: he was reproaching him with corrective intent

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the special status of Imam Musa عليه السلام over his brother Abdullah?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام distinguishing between two sons, affirming a unique inner nearness and spiritual light in one of them. It is significant in the context of identifying the special rank of Imam Musa عليه السلام and indicating a distinction beyond mere biological relationship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad BinYahya, from Muhammad Bin Al-Husayn, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Fuzayl, from Tahir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘It was so that Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was blaming Abdullah, and admonishing him and exhorting him, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘What is preventing you from becoming like your brother (Musa<sup>asws</sup>), for, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I<sup>asws</sup> recognise the Light in his<sup>asws</sup> face’.
So Abdullah said, ‘Isn’t my father<sup>asws</sup> and his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> one, and my mother and his<sup>asws</sup> mother one?’
So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘He<sup>asws</sup> is from my<sup>asws</sup> self, and you are my<sup>asws</sup> son’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Fudayl from Tahir from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.).

He has said that abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) would blame ‘Abdallah, show him his anger and advise him saying, “What is the matter that you are not like your brother (Musa) By Allah, I observe light inhis face.”
‘Abdallah thensaid, “Why is it? Is my and his father and mother not the same?” Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) then said, “He from my soul and you are my son.”
